newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to limit number of oil exporters - Rodionov.
newsitem.headline: Russia to limit number of oil exporters - Rodionov.

text.p: Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said on Tuesday that the government was getting ready to limit the number of companies exporting crude oil.

Interfax news agency quoted him as saying in the oil-rich town of Kogalym in Western Siberia that the government was preparing a decree that would introduce order to oil exports and restrict the number of trading companies specialising in export deliveries abroad.
"Those who work correctly, instead of trying to make money out of thin air, will probably continue their activities," Rodionov was quoted as saying.
Interfax gave no information on whether Rodionov had mentioned crude oil export levels.
But he was quoted as saying that Russia's oil companies could not solely be responsible for all of Russia's oil exports.
Interfax quoted LUKoil LKOH.RTS President Vagit Alekperov as calling on the minister to give Russia's oil producers sole control over exports.
Kogalym, in the Khanty-Mansiisk district in Western Siberia's oil-bearing Tyumen region, is home to some of LUKoil's operations.
Alekperov, Rodionov and other Russian oil industry executives are in the region to discuss aspects of industry.
